facts.statement: payment has one revision (created 07:15:56Z, no change-cause). checkout also has one revision (created 07:15:55Z). Neither was rolled out near the 07:35Z alert.
The paymentFailure flag is ENABLED at variant 50%. It is the only one of 18 flags switched on. Its change time is not shown.
payment, checkout and flagd show no restarts, OOMKills, failed probes or warnings in the last 60 minutes. Namespace warnings come from other components.

payment logs 19-20 warn-level lines 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' (charge.js:48), first seen 07:33:31Z. In the same 15m window it received 50 Charge requests and completed 30, so about 40% failed.
payment's Charge spans carry error.type=Error with the same Invalid token message. The message propagates through checkout's Charge and PlaceOrder spans and to frontend's 422 / rpc status 13.
Error-level log searches return nothing for payment or checkout. The failures are logged at warn level, so an error-level alert or search misses them.
payment's server Charge errors begin at 07:34Z and the error ratio goes from 0.07 to 0.32 by 07:37. checkout's client-side Charge errors begin in the same minute and mirror payment's series.

payment's outbound client spans show no sustained errors. Its only error is a short flagd EventStream error (07:29-07:32) that ended before the Charge errors began. Charge p95 latency is flat at about 1.9 ms.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Read paymentFailure's targeting/variant rules in the flagd config. Compare error rates for gold vs non-gold charges in payment logs or spans.
hypotheses.statement: The flag's targeting rule is scoped to gold loyalty, so only gold users hit the path. This would explain why the failures are gold-only and why the rate is not exactly 50%.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check flagd configuration change history or the flag's modification timestamp, and align it with the first warn at 07:33:31Z.
hypotheses.statement: The flag was switched on at about 07:33Z, just before the burn.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Turn the flag off in flagd (lab), then watch service:sli_error_ratio:rate1m for payment and checkout, and check that Invalid token warns stop.
hypotheses.statement: Disabling paymentFailure stops the payment and checkout Charge errors and the error ratio returns to baseline.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare checkout's Charge client span attributes for failing and successful calls. Only do this if the flag check does not explain the failures.
hypotheses.statement: A checkout request-shape or token change would appear as differences in request attributes on checkout's Charge client spans for gold-loyalty users.

inferences.statement: payment is the origin and checkout is a symptom. The Invalid token error is raised in payment's charge function, and checkout only re-reports it.
checkout is not the trigger. Its deployment is unchanged and it logs no errors of its own, so the burn is downstream of payment.

The paymentFailure flag is the most likely cause. It is the only enabled fault toggle, the failure rate (about 40%) is in the range of a 50% variant, and no code or rollout change explains the timing.

root_causes.cause: Charge path rejects charges with 'Invalid token' for gold-loyalty users, consistent with the paymentFailure flag (ENABLED, 50%) being on in flagd. This is the only enabled flag, and no payment code or rollout change occurred.

The paymentFailure flag change (or its targeting rule, which would explain the gold-only scope) was made in flagd's configuration and is not visible in the data. Its change history needs to be checked to confirm the timing.

Checkout sends malformed or unexpected tokens to payment, triggering the rejections. This is unlikely because checkout's deployment is unchanged and its errors are pass-through, but it has not been ruled out by request-level comparison.

diagnosis.summary: payment (lab) is failing about 24% of requests (about 40% of Charge calls in the last 15m). Its Charge handler throws 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' starting about 07:33-07:34Z. Checkout and frontend only relay that error, and checkout's own logs and deployment are clean. payment and checkout each have a single unchanged revision, and no pod restarts or warning events line up with the burn. The one enabled fault flag is paymentFailure at 50%, which is the most likely trigger. Its switch-on time is not yet confirmed, and the gold-only scope suggests its targeting rules should be checked. Mitigation: disable or revert the paymentFailure flag in flagd and confirm the payment error ratio drops.

alternatives.why_not: payment and checkout each have a single unchanged revision (created 07:15Z), so there is no earlier release to roll back to and no release near the 07:33Z onset.
No restarts, OOMKills, failed probes or warnings exist for payment, checkout or flagd, and the errors are deterministic 'Invalid token' rejections, not a stuck process.
Latency is flat (about 1.9 ms p95) and the failures are application-level rejections, not capacity shortfall.

plan.no_action_reason: Cause is the paymentFailure flag in flagd. A human should check flagd change history for its switch-on time and gold-loyalty targeting, then disable or revert it and verify payment and checkout error ratios drop.
plan.summary: No automated action is proposed. The payment Charge failures (about 40% of gold-loyalty charges) are most likely caused by the paymentFailure flag (ENABLED, 50%) in flagd, which none of the available actions can change. A human should disable or revert that flag and confirm the payment error ratio returns to baseline.

facts.statement: checkout's 5m error ratio rose from 0.073 at 07:34:03Z to 0.281 at 07:36:03Z and was 0.350 at 07:37:06Z.

checkout's only client spans with error status are PaymentService/Charge. Other checkout client spans (currency, product catalog, cart) show no errors, and no email, shipping or kafka spans appear in the error results.
payment's server-side Charge error rate starts around 07:34Z. Its 5m error ratio rose from 0.138 at 07:34:16Z to 0.322 at 07:36:16Z.
payment p95 latency stayed between 1.9 and 2.3 ms over the 3 hours, including during the spike, so its failures are fast, not slow.

All 17 failing checkout traces in the last 30m carry the token error at payment, and it reaches frontend-proxy as HTTP 422. Payment has 20 error traces in the last hour, all with the same message, first around 07:33Z.
Payment logs 20 warn lines with the token message between 07:33:31Z and 07:36:38Z. Error-level logs in payment are empty.
The flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 50%, and it is the only flag on out of 18.
checkout and payment each have a single revision from 07:15-07:16Z, with no rollout or restart in the window. Checkout's own spans are fast and its logs are clean.
flagd's error ratio is 0.0, apart from a single small EventStream error series (about 0.0035) that starts at 07:32 and is before the payment spike.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check flagd or the flag store's change history and last-modified time for paymentFailure, and confirm the change lands at about 07:33Z.
hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag was switched on around 07:33Z, which explains the start of the failures.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare payment Charge success rates split by demo.user_context.loyalty_level, and read the payment charge.js code path that emits the message.
hypotheses.statement: The token message is the injected failure's text, not a real validation bug. Non-gold users should keep succeeding while gold users fail.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare payment's Charge error ratio to the paymentFailure variant over the same window, and check the share of checkout requests that reach Charge.
hypotheses.statement: The observed ~0.35 checkout error ratio is consistent with a 50% payment failure rate applied to the share of checkouts that call Charge.

inferences.statement: payment is the origin of checkout's errors. Checkout is a symptom, since its failures match payment's Charge server errors in timing and size and no other dependency shows error spans.
No code or config rollout caused the burn. The likely trigger is a runtime change, either the paymentFailure flag or a payment behaviour change.

root_causes.cause: Charge calls fail hard (about half of them, per the paymentFailure 50% flag) with the 'Invalid token ... loyalty_level=gold' error. The likely trigger is the paymentFailure flag enabled in flagd, which makes payment fail deliberately. Checkout's order path surfaces these as 422s.

A payment-side token-validation defect that rejects gold-tier users, not an injected failure. Unconfirmed: the same symptom would appear, but the trigger would be a code or config change in payment rather than the flag.

diagnosis.summary: checkout's ErrorBudgetBurn (about 23.75% failing over 5m) is a symptom. Every failing checkout trace fails inside its call to payment, where payment returns 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' (logged at warn). Payment's server-side Charge error rate rises in step with checkout's, starting around 07:33-07:34Z, and payment latency stays flat, so these are fast hard failures. No rollout touched checkout or payment. The only enabled flag is paymentFailure at 50%, which fits the timing and magnitude. Mitigation: disable paymentFailure in flagd, or roll back payment's config, then confirm checkout's error ratio drops. Checkout itself and its other dependencies are not implicated.

alternatives.why_not: Neither checkout nor payment has a revision change in the window (ev_02097c5d1aa5070b, ev_d5ec1917fa4a6270), so there is no bad release to roll back to. The payment fault comes from a flag, not a pod template.

Payment's failures are fast and deterministic (p95 flat at 1.9-2.3 ms, ev_f4f293fec8a95dc8, and only warn-level token errors, ev_e9fa75388860d2fd). Nothing suggests a stuck or leaking process, so a restart would not stop the 50% failure rate.
Failures are hard rejections, not capacity shortfall or latency. Adding replicas would not reduce the flag-driven error rate.
Chosen. The fix sits in flagd (turn off paymentFailure), which is outside the actions I can propose.
